(a) Extension.—Notwithstanding section 2701 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2005 (division B of Public Law 108–375; 118 Stat. 2116), the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2601 of that Act, shall remain in effect until October 1, 2009, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2010, whichever is later. 
    (b) Table.—The table referred to in subsection (a) is as follows:
Army National Guard: Extension of 2005 Project Authorization





StateInstallation or LocationProjectAmount
CaliforniaDublinReadiness Center, Add/Alt (ADRS)$11,318,000

fable.w: This section only extends an existing military construction project authorization for an Army National Guard readiness center in California. The mention of a state location and the National Guard could suggest state involvement, but no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is provided. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2601 of that Act, shall remain in effect until October 1, 2009

opus.w: The section extends the deadline on a 2005 Army National Guard construction project authorization in Dublin, California, and nothing more. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The "State" column in the table only names where the project is located. It does not bring a state into any federal decision.
opus.b: This section only extends a military construction authorization. Words like "State" in the table or "Readiness Center" might look relevant, but no outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to comment on any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section merely extends an authorization for military construction funds and lists specific projects and amounts. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government (such as state governments, the public, or experts) in the decision-making process. The mention of 'Army National Guard' and 'State' refers to the location/beneficiary of the funds, not to a participatory mechanism.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the projects are for the Army National Guard (which has state ties), there is implicit participation. However, the text itself only lists appropriations and project authorizations. It does not describe any process of consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. The National Guard members or state officials are not described as participating in the decision-making process within this specific text; they are merely the beneficiaries or location of the funded projects.
